extracted.intended_audience: Reuters newsroom staff (journalists, editors, television producers, photographers)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and operational standards for Reuters journalists covering video/television stories and for handling corrections, refiles, repeats, kills and embargoes across Reuters products. Includes sourcing, image handling, conflict-of-interest, and Lynx Editor procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy means that our images and stories must reflect reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters is transparent about errors. We correct them promptly and clearly, whether in a story, a caption, a graphic or a script.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is the essence of our reputation as a 'stateless' global news organisation and fundamental to the trust that allows us to report impartially from all sides of a conflict or dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest or situations that could give rise to a perception of a conflict; independence stems from Reuters' structure and journalists' duty to avoid conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Neutrality is a hallmark of our news brand and allows us to work on all sides of an issue, conflict or dispute without any agenda other than accurate, fair reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always strive for balance and freedom from bias in reporting and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrity requires us to adhere to the highest ethical standards of our profession and to the values enshrined in The Reuters Trust Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must accept responsibilities, adhere to professional standards in personal conduct, exhibit high personal integrity and reveal conflicts of interest to a manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core journalist dos and don'ts
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of mandatory behaviours: always hold accuracy sacrosanct; always correct an error openly; always strive for balance and freedom from bias; always reveal a conflict of interest to a manager; always respect privileged information; always protect their sources; always guard against putting their opinion in a news story; never fabricate or plagiarise; never alter a still or moving image beyond the requirements of normal image enhancement; never pay for a story and never accept a bribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are non-negotiable daily practices; violations undermine Reuters Trust Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image and video manipulation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Never alter a still or moving image beyond the requirements of normal image enhancement; never manipulate or add/remove the contents of video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do only what is minimally necessary to improve technical quality. Audio must never be added which may affect the editorial interpretation of a sequence or story. Identify when using file and never misrepresent source, location or date of video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and identification of third-party video
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripts and shot-lists must be clear as to the source of any video material used, whether from Reuters, an allied broadcaster, amateur video, or third party which may have a political or commercial agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit phrasing such as 'video provided by the environmental group Greenpeace shows ...', 'video downloaded from a Web site known to be used by the group purports to show ...' or 'amateur video obtained by Reuters ...'. Consult news editors before using third-party footage where copyright or authenticity may be an issue. If unable to verify what video purports to show or when it was shot, say so in scripts/shot-lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal access and copyright vigilance
rubrics_metrics.description: We must be vigilant to ensure we have legal access to third-party material, for example in using appropriate Reuters forms in purchasing amateur or freelance video, both for news and archive purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source material as per guidance and be circumspect about assertions regarding third-party material; when necessary, purchase rights and use the proper forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment, junkets and gifts policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept 'junkets' from corporate/showbiz entities to cover stories at their expense; we never accept bribes and we do not accept gifts beyond those of nominal value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If we think it is a story we should generally pay our own travel. If travel with other entities is the only safe way to get to a story (e.g., military embed), disclose that in the script and consult editors about any implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of restricted or organised coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Organised news events should be identified as such (e.g., 'the CEO was speaking at a live media event organised by the company').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restricted from going to areas or prevented from asking questions, make this clear in copy. If restrictions would make coverage slanted, consult higher editorial management and be ready to refuse to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging camera presence effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere presence of television cameras can affect what happens in the area being filmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone is demonstrating something for us, say so; if a protest occurs in response to our arrival, state that. Example phrasing: 'residents protested at the scene of the attack after journalists arrived in the area.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabrication or plagiarism in video stories
rubrics_metrics.description: We never fake, fabricate or plagiarise a story. Video stories must not be shot, edited or scripted in a way which misleads the viewer or subscriber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the story accurately and strive to record events exactly as they happen. As neutral observers, play no part beyond documenting. Use wide shots and close-ups to convey scale when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of file material and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: We must identify when we use file and never misrepresent the source, location or date of video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write own stories based on newsgathering; when using another source for information, identify that source. Do not lift sections of copy from other news sources, websites or online encyclopedias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling graphic, sexual and sensitive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters may distribute graphic/sexual/sensitive material for historical accuracy and context, but extreme content (executions, torture, graphic sexual scenes) requires consultation with a senior editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alert clients boldly in scripts and slates that graphic/explicit content follows so they may shield their newsroom staff. Consider staff sensitivities and allow removal of staff who may be impacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting sources and resisting handing over raw material
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not divulge the sources of our content to officials and we resist handing over our raw video to governmental, police or military authorities unless the physical safety of our journalists is under immediate threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any requests/demands to hand over material must be referred immediately to senior editorial management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer ethical or legal doubts to higher editorial management
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to codify every ethical dilemma; different laws may apply in different countries. If in any doubt about a situation, refer the matter to higher editorial management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unsure about filming children, secret filming, or other legal/ethical issues, seek guidance from senior editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections ethos
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is totally honest about errors. We rectify them promptly and clearly. We do not disguise or bury mistakes in subsequent updates or stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat stories only when running them without change from the original. Many corrections can be prevented by basic checks (day of week, names, figures). See Avoiding Errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error classification: kill, corrected, refile, repeat
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters recognises three classes of errors and has set up separate procedures: STORY WITHDRAWN (kill) for stories totally wrong or fundamentally flawed; CORRECTED for substantive factual errors that alter meaning or credibility; REFILE for minor factual errors/typos that do not affect investment decisions or understanding; REPEAT for stories previously appeared and reissued unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision on kill/correction/refile/repeat rests with the editing desk or specialist editor. Use refiles for minor errors; corrections for substantive ones; kills only after consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trashlines/advisory lines mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Trashlines or advisory lines at the top of the text are mandatory for all withdrawals, corrections, refiles and repeats and must be filed within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trashline should say exactly why a story is being killed, corrected, refiled or repeated. All trashlines on refiles and corrections must include the word 'corrects' or 'correcting'. They serve transparency and routing to some customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections procedures in Lynx Editor (stories <24 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: For stories published less than 24 hours ago: find the story in a Publish basket or search, click Correct, which opens the story and automatically keeps the same USN, adds Message Type A, adds (CORRECTED) in the slugline and CORRECTED- headline tag before the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should write a corrected version and transfer to a regional editing desk for editing and publishing. The correction functionality will publish the correction by replacing the original item on the same USN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alerts/Newsbreaks correction via 'Correct Chain' function
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting an alert and clicking Correct Chain opens a 'Chain Correction' dialog allowing correction of all alerts on a new USN or selecting specific alerts for correction, refile, repeat or delete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: 'All' will open file and add CORRECTED-; 'Custom' lets you choose action per alert. The Correct button allows drafting but does not publish. Reporters should transfer corrected alerts to regional editing desk for publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections procedures in Lynx Editor (stories >24 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: For stories published more than 24 hours ago: follow similar steps but you must change the USN to publish the correction on a new USN and then go back and delete the old item using 'Historical Delete'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlock the USN field (CTRL+SHIFT+S), erase the old USN, save to generate a new USN, change message type to S, add (CORRECTED) in slugline and CORRECTED- before headline. Desk editors must then use Historical Delete on the original story and enter the original published date/time in exact format DD-MM-YYYY:HH:MM:SS.00 using LOCAL TIME.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical delete procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To remove original story after issuing a correction on a new USN, desk editors must use 'Historical Delete' and enter the published date/time in DD-MM-YYYY:HH:MM:SS.00 format (LOCAL TIME).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the offending story remains on desktop services after Historical Delete, email Editorial Iteam with a screengrab including USN and published time for removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blogs correction and update conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a blog post needs a correction, strike out the incorrect material, then immediately afterwards write the corrected word or phrase in brackets. Add CORRECTED after the headline of the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For relatively minor corrections, simply write the correct word or phrase after the struck-through section. It's acceptable to fix minor misspellings without leaving a record. If a post is updated, add UPDATED after the headline and place the update in brackets where it belongs or link to an updated story. If correcting a headline, add a correction line at bottom of post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official corrections format
rubrics_metrics.description: We only describe a correction as official if a source has acknowledged that the original information was wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a DIFFERENT USN from the original Alert; type CORRECTED-(OFFICIAL)- in upper case before the text and headline; delete the original Alert; chain the Newsbreak to the Alert using CORRECTED-(OFFICIAL)-. Do not put an A in the Ref/Msg type box of the header field. Example shown in handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refiles procedures and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Refiles allow Reuters to correct minor factual errors without burying them in repeats. Slugs for refiles and corrections use (CORRECTED) as part of the slug. The headline should begin with REFILE- followed immediately by the headline text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be an advisory line (trashline) above the story text telling readers what is being corrected; follow the same trashline procedures as for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeats procedures and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeats are reserved for stories that have previously appeared on a Reuters news service and do not contain errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeats should always be issued with (REPEAT) at the end of the slug line and RPT- at the front of the headline. There must be an advisory line above the story text explaining why the story is being repeated (e.g., 'Repeats to widen distribution'). Repeats or updates should never be used to overwrite mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kills/Withdrawals procedures and advisories
rubrics_metrics.description: If a story is suspected of being wrong and cannot be immediately confirmed, send an Advisory to clients with a different USN. If a story is fundamentally flawed, send an ADVISORY saying the story is wrong and withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory must state reasons for the withdrawal and have same address codes as original, same USN, message type R and topic code WDW. Include GMT time/date when original item ran and its USN explicitly. Bureau chiefs may need to write an Incident Report. Do not kill stories without consulting a desk editor and specialist editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect-story handling (advisory vs correction vs kill)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a story is suspected wrong but not confirmed, send an ADVISORY. If it needs only a correction, send CORRECTED with the same USN and A in header; if fundamentally flawed, send advisory and kill with message type R and topic code WDW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include storyline: advisory line/trashline explaining reason, story number, date, time, and whether substitute story follows; consult editorial team and follow deletion procedures for old items as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo types: transmission and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Two types of embargoes: a TRANSMISSION EMBARGO restricts publication to all clients until a specified time; a PUBLICATION EMBARGO transmits immediately to media clients only with restrictions preventing them publishing/broadcasting until a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication embargo requires publishing to media clients with notice, then creating a transmission embargo copy to desktop clients using Lynx Editor embargo function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimising risk of embargo breaks (marking and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureaux transferring embargoed material to an editing desk must clearly mark it as embargoed in two places in UPPER CASE: in the slugline and in the comment line in Lynx Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example slug: BC-BALDONIA-SOLDIERS (EMBARGOED). Comment line should state 'EMBARGOED FOR RELEASE AT 2301 GMT APRIL 28'. When setting publication embargo, add EMB code to Topic code line, ensure only relevant media product codes are present, delete other product codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to set and remove embargo in Lynx Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: To place a TRANSMISSION embargo: open story, click Set in embargo field, specify date/time (defaults to GMT), click Set to save. To revise click Edit; to remove click Remove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When embargo is set, Publish button changes to Embargo button to transfer story to Embargo basket for automatic publishing at expiry. For publication embargo, publish to media clients with embargo notice then copy story for transmission embargo to desktop clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accidental release of embargoed material
rubrics_metrics.description: If embargoed material is released accidentally to screen services, this material must NOT be deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue an advisory with the same USN (use S message type) to add an advisory to the bottom of the story explaining inadvertent release. Do not delete the accidentally released material since that may advantage those who saw it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mending fences after embargo breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: After an embargo break, the bureau or reporting team must inform relevant editing, the supplying organisation, and if merited, regulatory authorities such as stock exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologise, explain steps to prevent recurrence, and write a letter to the affected organisation. In most cases an incident report is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — RICs (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct when the RIC used is not that of the company in the news (e.g., links news to wrong company) or links to a blank data page; data errors generally require correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a RIC belongs to no other company and links to a blank data page, the story should be refiled to remove the dead RIC and replace it with an active RIC. If a RIC belonging to another company is mistakenly used, a correction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — data and numbers (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly every error that involves a number requires a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: million vs billion errors; wrong prices almost always merit corrections; mistakes in numbers that alter meaning or significance should be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — dates and time periods (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct wrong dates, months or years in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes dateline errors and days of the week in the first paragraph which often can be addressed with a refile unless the meaning changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — quotes (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any error in a quote that changes the meaning of the sentence must be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unacceptable to drop the quote from an update instead of issuing a correction. Minor quote errors that don't change meaning may be refiles, but changing meaning requires correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — prices (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong price for a stock, bond or other asset requires a correction rather than an update (unless price legitimately changed while filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also correct mistakes in the direction of price changes (e.g., saying a stock rose instead of fell).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — background, descriptions and analyses (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions, analyses or explanations that are erroneous should be corrected even if republished from a previous story or if they are not of primary importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: 'The second paragraph erroneously described XYZ Co as the largest widget maker in the world. XYZ Co is the second largest behind QRS Corp.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — proper names (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of people, places, companies and organisations should be corrected when a misspelling creates confusion or when an erroneous name has been substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a refile to correct obvious typos in proper names (e.g., 'President Georeg Bush'). If substitution changes meaning (e.g., wrong person named), correction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — dropped word (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a missing word changes the meaning of a sentence, a correction is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a dropped word does not change meaning use a refile to add it; but when meaning changes (e.g., 'He was found guilty' vs 'He was found not guilty'), correction required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to correct — time references (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections of time references should carry advisory lines noting the corrected time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample advisory: 'Corrects month measured by housing data to June instead of July.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refile — RICs linking to blank/inactive symbols (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for wrong RICs only when the symbol used belongs to no other company and links to a blank data page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline example: 'Refiles to correct inactive stock symbol in paragraph 4.' If a RIC belongs to another company, a correction is required instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refile — dateline errors (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for errors in datelines, including location and date, unless either would have an important bearing on the meaning of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Corrects dateline from FRANKFURT to Brussels' would be a correction; simple dateline typos may be refiled if they don't change significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refile — day-of-week errors in lead (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile when the wrong day of the week appears in the lead sentence, unless the mistake would distort the significance of the story or applies to a future day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: 'Corrects day in first paragraph to Tuesday from Monday.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refile — simple time conversion errors (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for simple time conversions when the time being converted is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Corrects time in paragraph 3 to 1350 GMT from 1550 GMT.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to refile — spelling and typographical errors (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for typographical errors of common words or most spelling mistakes in proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example trashline: 'Fixes typo in 10th paragraph' or 'Corrects spelling of Greenspan in final paragraph.' For misspelt names that cause confusion, consider correction instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special note on Alerts (appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes in Alerts raise the special issue of timings; many errors that would merit refiles are usually better left unaddressed in Alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a refile is deemed necessary, let the Alert with the mistake stand and issue a refile that would stand side by side with the original. Any mistake involving a number should still be corrected in Alerts. Bureau, reporter or editor should not independently decide handling of Alert mistakes; refer to editing desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captioning and photo credit practice (implied from examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo captions should identify subject/action, provide context (what/when/where), and include credit and country in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in handbook show captions like: 'An employee of Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd shows the media the company's new 32-Gigabit NAND flash memory card ... REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon (SOUTH KOREA)'. The Chief Photographer carries responsibility for the file from the region in question.
